plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, bidding exactly my true value ($30) is the dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win, while bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, there's no benefit to shading my bid. I'll bid my true value of $30.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy: I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid, and bidding my true value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid losses when it's not. Since this is a one-shot game with no history to learn from, I'll bid exactly my value of $28.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since the price I pay is determined by the second-highest bid (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds what others bid) and never overpay (since I'd only pay the second-highest bid, which would be less than my value if I win). Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I'm forced to pay close to my bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $24, so I'll bid exactly that.
